The servers of a platform, kept as the model describes them, with Ansible: ansible/ prepares a new Debian server (task bootstrap, once, as root) and keeps every server up to date (task plan shows what would change, task apply changes it): an admin user that signs in with your SSH key and no password, no root login, the firewall, automatic security updates, and Docker with the network the platform's services share. The secrets are in secrets/, encrypted with SOPS and age: task secrets:init makes your key, task secrets:edit changes them. Your own tasks go in ansible/roles/local, which esquadro never rewrites.

```esquadro
blueprint server
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admin_user` | string | `"admin"` | The user Ansible and you sign in as: it has sudo, root has no login. |
| `ssh_key` | string | `"~/.ssh/id_ed25519"` | Your SSH key, which Ansible and the tasks sign in with; the admin user gets its public half, the same path with .pub. |
| `timezone` | string | `"UTC"` | The servers' time zone. |

```esquadro
blueprint server {
  admin_user "admin"
}
```

## Slots

Other blueprints add code at these points (see [Writing a blueprint](/esquadro/writing-blueprints/#slots)).

| Slot | |
|---|---|
| `server.roles` | Roles of ansible/site.yml after base and docker, as YAML list items indented by four spaces, e.g. "    - caddy". |
| `server.vars` | Variables of ansible/group_vars/all/platform.yml, as YAML at the top level. |
| `server.ports` | Ports the firewall lets in besides SSH, as YAML list items indented by two spaces, e.g. "  - 443". |
| `server.secrets` | Secrets of secrets/platform.sops.yaml, as YAML lines "key: value" with a comment above; the value generate makes task secrets:init write a random one, an empty one is yours to fill. |
| `server.tasks` | Tasks of Taskfile.esquadro.yml, as YAML indented by two spaces. |
| `server.plan` | Commands task plan runs before Ansible's, as YAML list items indented by six spaces, e.g. "      - task: tofu:plan". |
| `server.apply` | Commands task apply runs before Ansible's, as task plan's. |
| `server.readme` | Sections of README.md, in Markdown. |
